title: Minimum Difficulty of a Job Schedule
summary: Given an array of job difficulties and a number of days, find the minimum total difficulty by scheduling jobs such that each day has at least one job, and the difficulty of a day is the highest job difficulty on that day.
statement: Given an array of job difficulties and a number of days, find the minimum total difficulty by scheduling jobs such that each day has at least one job, and the difficulty of a day is the highest job difficulty on that day. Return -1 if a valid schedule cannot be made.
constraints: Jobs must be completed in the given order over exactly d days.
Every day receives at least one consecutive block; its difficulty is the maximum job in that block.
Return the minimum sum of daily difficulties, or -1 when there are fewer jobs than days.
hints: Partition an ordered prefix into completed days.
For each final day endpoint, scan its possible start backward while maintaining that day’s maximum.
Add the previous-day optimum before the chosen start and minimize.
Every exact-day schedule has one final block, so testing all starts is exhaustive and subproblems are independent.
editorial: Dynamic programming stores the minimum difficulty for scheduling each prefix in an exact number of days. Scanning a final block backward updates its maximum in constant time per candidate. Impossible states remain infinite, which enforces nonempty days. The oracle independently enumerates all combinations of day-boundary cuts.

tests.explanation: Putting the first five jobs on day one and the last job on day two costs six plus one.
Three jobs cannot fill four nonempty days.
